issues.legal_issue: Dropping a proceeding intended to prevent a breach of peace does not by itself require dropping a separate proceeding concerning possession.
material_facts: A proceeding concerning possession was initiated after the appellant alleged that he had been removed from the disputed portion of the house.

The proceeding intended to prevent a breach of peace was dropped, and the Magistrate then dropped the possession proceeding on the ground that there was no longer an apprehension of a breach of peace.
The High Court agreed with that reasoning.
issues.conclusion: The dropping of the proceeding intended to prevent a breach of peace did not justify dropping the separate possession proceeding, because the proceedings serve different purposes.
issues.legal_principle: Proceedings under Section 107 CrPC are preventive measures directed to public peace and tranquillity; proceedings under Section 145 CrPC concern disputes about possession of land or water. As explained in Madhu Limaye v. Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Monghyr, the preventive nature of the former does not make its continuation a prerequisite to the latter.

predicates.possession_dispute_proceeding: A party initiated a proceeding to resolve a dispute about actual possession of property.
predicates.separate_peace_prevention_proceeding_dro: A separate proceeding intended to prevent a breach of peace was discontinued.

issues.definition: When a possession dispute proceeding is separate from a discontinued peace-prevention proceeding, the possession dispute proceeding may continue.

issues.legal_issue: A pending civil suit does not automatically bar a possession proceeding when title is not disputed and the dispute concerns actual possession.
material_facts: The appellant had a civil suit for an injunction pending, but he alleged that he had already been removed from possession before the status quo order was made.
The respondent acknowledged that the parties were co-owners and claimed the property was ancestral; the Court found no dispute about title.
The dispute concerned possession, including whether the appellant had been forcibly or wrongfully dispossessed within the relevant period.
The Magistrate and High Court treated the civil remedy as a reason to drop the possession proceeding without deciding the possession issue.
issues.conclusion: The civil suit did not justify rejecting the possession application. The courts below failed to exercise their jurisdiction by not determining the alleged recent forcible or wrongful dispossession, and their orders could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 145 CrPC, a Magistrate may address a dispute concerning possession where the issue is possession rather than title. Ram Sumer Puri Mahant v. State of U.P. states the normal rule that a civil suit, particularly one based on title where possession is being examined and interim protection is available, ordinarily prevents parallel criminal proceedings. The Court held that this rule does not apply where title is not disputed and the issue is whether a party was forcibly or wrongfully dispossessed within the relevant period.

rule.if: possession_dispute_proceeding and civil_suit_pending and title_not_in_dispute and dispute_is_about_actual_possession and recent_forcible_dispossession_alleged

predicates.possession_dispute_proceeding: A party initiated a proceeding to resolve a dispute about actual possession of property.
predicates.civil_suit_pending: A civil action concerning the property was pending while the possession proceeding was considered.
predicates.title_not_in_dispute: The parties did not dispute their entitlement to the property or their status as co-owners.
predicates.dispute_is_about_actual_possession: The parties' disagreement concerned who possessed the property, rather than who held title.
predicates.recent_forcible_dispossession_alleged: A party alleged that they had recently been forcibly or wrongfully removed from possession.

issues.definition: When a possession proceeding and a civil suit are pending, title is not disputed, and recent forcible dispossession is alleged, the possession proceeding must be decided on the possession issue.
